key_insight: β-TeO3 is predicted to be an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with exceptionally high work functions approaching 8 eV, enabled by favorable defect chemistry and surface electronic structure.
engineering_relevance: This makes β-TeO3 a promising material for hole injection/extraction layers and transparent electrodes in optoelectronic devices, including solar cells and LEDs.
method: First-principles defect calculations to identify shallow donors and compensating defects.
Surface-specific work-function evaluation across multiple low-index nonpolar facets.
Thermodynamic assessment of oxygen-vacancy formation under varying O chemical potential.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a band gap above 3 eV and work functions up to ~8 eV, with shallow donor impurities and surface O vacancies quantified by first-principles evaluation.
watch_item: Performance may degrade if oxygen-vacancy formation is not tightly controlled at surfaces, since these defects lower the work function and can compensate carriers.
paper_title: Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
